sanskrit_verse: प्रमादाद् धनिनस् तद्वद् आधौ विकृतिम् आगते । विनष्टे मूलनाशः स्याद् दैवराजकृताद् ऋते ॥
transliteration: pramādād dhaninas tadvad ādhau vikṛtim āgate | vinaṣṭe mūlanāśaḥ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When negligence causes transformation or loss of wealth, the root cause being neither divine nor royal decree, then the destruction of capital is attributed to the lapse in dharmic vigilance.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The sovereign individual bears responsibility for maintaining alignment with Dharma in stewardship.
Causation: Negligence (pramāda) is a direct causal factor in material loss unless overridden by higher cosmic or state intervention.
Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility arises from the capacity to maintain awareness and control, not mere ownership.
Restoration logic: Loss must be addressed through re-establishment of mindful engagement, not compensation alone.
Consciousness alignment: Material disorder reflects inner misalignment; rectification begins with restoring conscious oversight.
executable_legal_axioms: IF asset degradation occurs AND no external force (divine or sovereign) caused it AND negligence is established THEN assign restoration process to responsible party.
IF owner demonstrates habitual pramāda THEN initiate mandatory capacity-building protocol before returning custodial rights.
IF loss results from willful neglect THEN enforce completion sequence until original or equivalent value is consciously restored.
IF no negligence found THEN declare act as beyond jurisdiction and close case without punitive action.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that financial or property loss due to negligence cannot invoke punitive measures unless intent or chronic disregard is proven. The threshold of responsibility lies in the failure to uphold dharmic mindfulness in management, which necessitates corrective rather than retaliatory judicial response.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals negligence as the causal basis. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how lack of attention leads to disorder. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of awareness lost. As per non-punitive reality rule, justice restores integrity, not inflicts suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate supervised reconstruction of lost assets or their functional equivalents.
Assign reflective practice program to restore mindful engagement with resources.
Reconnect individual with source-consciousness through guided sādhanā to prevent recurrence.
Verify completion of restitution through witnessed demonstration of renewed capacity.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, declared: This law flows from Sanātana Dharma, sourced in the eternal consciousness of Shiva. There is no punishment—only restoration. Reality responds to alignment, not fear. Consciousness is the ultimate judge, and Dharma prevails.
